domain_002:n1.prompt:
You are helping me set up the payment step for purchasing a domain. Goal: prepare a checkout flow so a human can review and pay for the domain purchase quote — you must not complete or approve the payment yourself.

Before starting, ask me for any missing inputs: the domain name being purchased, the exact price/currency to charge, and which payments provider I want to use (the {{vendor}} product for this arena — e.g. a hosted checkout or an order/transaction API).

Actions to take:
1. Using your configured credentials for {{vendor}}, create a checkout session (or equivalent order/transaction) that presents the domain price for my approval and payment. Use the appropriate grounded operation for the chosen {{vendor}} — either the generic write/execute tool, or the documented REST endpoint if one is grounded for that vendor — described in words if no exact endpoint is specified.
2. Set the line item description clearly to reference the domain name and purchase purpose.
3. Confirm the session/order is created in a pending state awaiting payment, and retrieve the resulting checkout link or reference ID.
4. Do NOT submit payment, confirm the order, or mark it as paid — that action requires my explicit approval.

When done, report back: the {{vendor}} checkout/session reference or ID, the payment link (if applicable), the domain name and price shown, and confirmation that it is awaiting payment. Present this clearly and then stop for human sign-off — do not proceed further until I explicitly approve and complete the payment myself.

domain_002:n2.prompt:
You are helping me register and pay for a domain through {{vendor}}, our chosen domain registrar. Before starting, ask me for: the exact domain name (including TLD) I want to register, my {{vendor}} account status (confirm I have configured credentials), and the registrant contact details to use (name, email, address, phone) unless privacy/WHOIS protection is enabled by default. 

Steps to perform: (1) Use {{vendor}}'s documented availability/search API or dashboard to confirm the domain is available and pull the published price for registration and renewal (not just a teaser first-year rate) for this TLD. (2) Prepare the full registration request — domain name, contact/registrant details, requested nameservers (leave default unless I specify Cloudflare's), and payment method tied to my configured Stripe/billing setup — as a draft summary for my review. (3) Do NOT submit the purchase or charge payment yet. Present me the draft (domain, price breakdown, renewal price, contact info, nameservers) and stop for human sign-off. 

Once I explicitly approve, submit the registration/purchase via {{vendor}}'s domain creation API or dashboard. Because this action is asynchronous, after submission poll {{vendor}}'s domain status/lookup API (or dashboard) periodically to verify the registration has completed and is active — this confirmation may take time and remains a human step to finally verify receipt if {{vendor}} sends email confirmation outside the API. 

Report back: whether the domain was available, the exact price quoted (registration + renewal), the draft contact/config details I approved, the submission result, and the current verified registration status (pending/active) with any next steps needed (e.g., DNSSEC setup, nameserver changes).

domain_002:n3.prompt:
You are helping me complete the DNS/SSL provisioning step for a domain I just purchased and registered at Name.com, with payment already processed via Stripe. Please act as an async step: kick off the work, then poll/verify until it's confirmed complete, since results may not be instant.

If not already provided, ask me for: (1) the exact domain name, (2) which edge platform I'm using as {{vendor}} for DNS/SSL/edge routing, and (3) the target service or origin the domain should point to (e.g., my deployed app or backend).

Using my configured credentials, do the following:
1. Add the domain to {{vendor}} (or confirm it's already added) so it can manage DNS.
2. Via the {{vendor}} execute tool/API, create the necessary DNS records (A/AAAA/CNAME as appropriate) pointing the domain to the target service.
3. Enable or confirm automatic, auto-renewing TLS/SSL for the domain, including wildcard coverage if applicable.
4. If this domain is meant to attach to a deployed service or act as a custom domain for a multi-tenant setup, configure that custom domain attachment/routing via {{vendor}} as well.
5. Poll {{vendor}}'s status (DNS propagation, SSL certificate issuance) until both DNS resolution and SSL are confirmed active — do not report success prematurely.

Done looks like: DNS records are live, SSL certificate is issued and auto-renewing, and the domain correctly resolves to the intended target over HTTPS.

Report back with: the DNS records created (type, name, value), SSL/certificate status, any custom domain/routing configuration applied, and confirmation timestamps from your verification polling. Flag any records or settings you could not create automatically so I can review them.
